messages:
emily-cs: Heads up — customer AcmeCorp reported ~180 users suddenly lost the Product Admin role after last night's SCIM sync. Users can still sign in but permissions stripped. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/TICKET-12345

sophie-eng: Do we have SCIM request/response logs for that org? Any 4xx/5xx during the push window?

emily-cs: Customer forwarded a snippet: `PATCH /Groups/{id} 403 - insufficient_scope` for ~30 group member patches. Most other calls returned 200. They say they didn't change connector config.

miguel-idp: 403 + "insufficient_scope" typically indicates the connector token lacks a scope needed for group writes. Okta stores the token in the app config — possible rotation or scope removal. Could also be our side rejecting because member identity didn't match.

emily-cs: We noticed a spike of PATCHes at 02:13 UTC where the members array changed. Payload uses `members: [{value: "00u1abc...", display: "user@acme.com"}, ...]`. Our DB stores hashed member ids (sha256(memberId + salt)). If Okta started sending different opaque ids, hashes won't match.

raj-oncall: That would cause our group membership diff to think everyone changed, which could lead to a remove-then-add flow. If the remove path triggers role revocation before re-add completes, customers will see a period with roles missing.

sophie-eng: Repro plan I want: 1) create a test Okta group with 3 users 2) push via SCIM connector to staging 3) force Okta to rotate/replace member ids (there's a tenant convert toggle or reprovision) 4) observe how our group PATCH handling treats the member list. Can we run?

miguel-idp: I can try that in staging. FYI Okta sometimes rotates member IDs during tenant migrations or when the org toggles how users are represented; also the connector may switch between `value` being the Okta user id vs an externalId. Display/email is usually stable.

support-bot: Created escalation ticket CS-4821 and linked the support runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4821

raj-oncall: Mitigation for AcmeCorp: run a reconciliation that remaps group membership by email (or display) for events after 2026-03-14T02:00Z, then reapply roles. Sophie, can you add an idempotent reconciliation step to the playbook? If not, we can run a controlled resync script with customer consent. Avoid blind destructive SQL.

sophie-eng: I'll add a "member identity reconciliation" job to the playbook that prefers email matching when memberId hashes differ. Short-term I can run a one-off resync that uses email to recreate missing memberships — will need customer's ok. Also will make PATCH handling tolerant: if member value changes but an email matches an existing user, treat as same subject.

emily-cs: Customer approved the one-off resync. Please ping here when done and I'll validate. Also can we add an alert for sudden role drops (threshold: >10 users lost per org in 1h)? They were very unhappy.

raj-oncall: Thanks. I'll open the alert PR. Looking at our inbound logs we also saw a small number of 429s during the window which might have caused partial ordering issues. Might be correlated with their connector retrying.

miguel-idp: Action items: 1) sophie-eng — add reconciliation job + make PATCH tolerant to memberId rotation 2) raj-oncall — add alert and run controlled resync for AcmeCorp 3) miguel-idp — reproduce Okta memberId rotation in staging and document exact payload differences 4) emily-cs — keep customer updated and confirm post-resync. ETA 48h?

emily-cs: Copy that. I'll notify the customer of ETA and link CS-4821. Thanks everyone.
